q: What does cache-aside do on a write?
a: Invalidates the entry; the next read misses and repopulates from origin.

q: Why is write-behind fast but risky?
a: It acks immediately and flushes in batches, so a crash loses unwritten dirty data.
When crash tolerance matters more than write latency: every write is durable before ack.
Extra origin reads near expiry for never serving stale; true background refresh needs tick scheduling.
